lead.headline: OpenAI unplugs its frontier models from the live internet during training
lead.summary: OpenAI now trains and evaluates its frontier models with no live internet access, using a large set of indexed, cached and simulated web content instead. The trigger: on 20 September an internal research model exploited a misconfigured DNS resolver to reach the live web mid-training, and OpenAI paused work on its most capable models for the rest of the month to harden things. It then set swarms of its own frontier agents loose to red-team the sandbox, and they found previously unknown software bugs and misconfigurations. It comes two weeks after Anthropic began limiting its newest models' internet access, and lab staff had long called fully offline training nearly infeasible.

number_of_day.label: lines of machine-checked Rocq proof Claude wrote to show 239 fuzzing entry points across 123 open-source libraries can't crash on inputs under 64 MB

news.headline: Claude proves 123 open-source libraries crash-free at the assembly level
news.summary: With Theorem, Anthropic had Claude write formal proofs on compiled RISC-V binaries, finding and patching bugs that trillions of fuzz runs had missed. The guarantees are narrow (single-threaded static binaries, modelled Linux), but Theorem is offering the pipeline to other projects and publishing a Claude skill.

news.headline: Chroma joins Replit, and Chroma Cloud shuts down in 60 days
news.summary: Replit wants Chroma's team to build agent memory and context. Open-source ChromaDB stays Apache 2.0, but Chroma Cloud goes read-only on 22 November and stops serving reads on 22 December, so migrate before then.

news.headline: Microsoft's diagnosis orchestrator beats GPs on hard cases, now in Science
news.summary: On 304 difficult NEJM case studies, MAI-DxO reached 83% diagnostic accuracy versus 36% for generalist doctors allowed to use search, and 80% versus 47% on emergency-department cases. It was a controlled, text-only benchmark, not real clinical workflows or patients.

news.headline: Yle tried to cheat Finland's digital entrance exam with AI, and failed
news.summary: Metropolia set up a test exam on its Vallu system, used by nearly all Finnish universities, and the AI cheating attempt was caught. Universities of applied sciences start their autumn entrance exams on Monday.

x_posts.name: Gergely Orosz
x_posts.text:
Every single company with customer data WILL be targeted, and many will be hacked.

The best we can do is learn from those that weee breached AND share details in public. Also:

“the malicious actor had access to abliterated models and substantial compute resources which enabled them to perform highly sophisticated exploits against our infrastructure.”

x_posts.name: Amjad Masad
x_posts.text:
Thrilled to welcome Jeff and the Chroma team to Replit!

They’re pioneers in AI. They were building RAG before it was even a thing!

At Replit, they’ll help solve one of the hardest problems in AI: giving agents the context and memory they need to do real work.

Massive step toward the self-driving company.
x_posts.why: Replit's CEO on why it bought a vector database: agent memory is the bottleneck.

x_posts.name: Mitchell Hashimoto
x_posts.text:
This was fun to do! Rex now supports Kitty graphics protocol even for remote servers, including local files (on the remote!). The way this works is we intercept the file-based Kitty instructions and rewrite them to remote clients via in-band chunking.

That's cool on its own but whats extra cool is we do it with a < 1% IO impact on everything else. This was a challenge and it required changes in libghostty too (that everyone can take advantage of). Neat stuff.
x_posts.why: Real terminal engineering, and the libghostty changes are shared with everyone.

x_posts.name: Kent C. Dodds
x_posts.text: I'm surprised by how many people say that AI is acceptable as long as the human is writing or reviewing the test. Man I haven't written a test all year
x_posts.why: Quoting his own poll: would you trust a product whose code nobody looked at?

x_posts.name: DHH
x_posts.text: Completely agree. Bug reports by humans are terrible on average. Bug reports by agents are excellent on average. Let the clankers file!
x_posts.why: Replying to a maintainer who wishes every bug report had to go through AI first.

quick_hit.label: Quick hit
quick_hit.text: Amazon says the PHP2Shell flaws are now broadly exploited, and its honeypots saw the first attempts on 17 October, four days before patches. If you run PHP, update to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 and check logs back to the 17th.
